description: Attention stall chain and the decision_status sub-state (W2, issue #1451). An unanswered re-request of an open attention record bumps the record's stall_count; the task's decision_status sub-state escalates at the thresholds below and returns to open when the answer arrives. The sub-state overlays the nine runtime states (task-transitions.json) and is written only by the protocol layer: the stall chain is the convergence point that writes 'blocked', and 'frozen' is released only by a resolved approval record. Enforced while the protocol.enforce switch is on (TEAMHARNESS_RUNTIME_CONFIG protocol section, TEAMHARNESS_PROTOCOL_ENFORCE env override); with the switch off request_attention keeps its pre-W2 idempotent-reuse behaviour and no stall or decision_status fields are written.

decision_options.rule: a kind=decision raise must carry options[] (1..10 {id,label} entries) while the switch is on; the check runs at raise time, before any write, notification or event (no half record). An explicit resolved=true close is exempt in BOTH switch states: it answers the record it closes, and that record's options (when present) were fixed at its own raise time
decision_options.enforce_on: a NEW decision raise without options[] is rejected (request_attention kind=decision requires options[]); kind=approval and the other kinds are unaffected
decision_options.enforce_off: a NEW decision raise without options[] succeeds — pre-W2 backward-compatible behaviour; such a record is answered in free text through the explicit close
decision_options.deployment_default: protocol.enforce defaults to false (off) — see switch.default; an unset key is pre-W2 behaviour. Flipping the switch on enforces NEW decision raises only: already-open records keep their shape and stay answerable in free text

legacy_records.definition: an unresolved kind=decision record without options — raised with the switch off or before this guard existed
legacy_records.strategy: answer in place, no migration: the record is closed through the explicit resolve path with a free-text answer (it has no options to echo); it is never rewritten, force-migrated, options-backfilled or marked legacy — the free-text answer is recorded as resolve provenance on the record itself (resolved / resolvedVia / resolvedBy / resolveEvidence / resolvedAt)
legacy_records.freeform_evidence: the dashboard close marks the free-text answer with evidence {"freeform": true} (TH-4); the matrix close keeps the answer text in the room and cites it in resolveEvidence

resolve_paths.matrix: the human answers in the task room; the room reply or command closes the record with resolvedVia=im_reply or im_command, resolvedBy, and resolveEvidence citing the room message. kind=approval additionally requires the trusted human runtime role (approval_requires_human) while the switch is on
resolve_paths.dashboard: TH-4 POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/attention/{taskId}/resolve — resolution is an option id OR free text (a legacy record can only be free text); free text requires evidence {"freeform": true} and a record that carries options rejects a text that matches no option id (resolution_not_an_option, 400); the close is recorded with resolvedVia=dashboard

decision_options.event_identity: the attention_raised event id fingerprints the record's stable identity (the creation-time fields as canonical JSON), not the post-write meta bytes — see signal-mapping.json id_rule, attention family (#1506)

attention_record_fields.stall_count: integer; written 0 on record creation (switch on), +1 per unanswered re-request of the open same-kind record (the idempotent reuse path), 0 again when the record is resolved; never written with the switch off

history_entry.actor: role:account of the resolving call (when known)

decision_status.history_written: on entering blocked/frozen, on leaving them back to open, and on a refused attempt to leave frozen (a refused entry carries from='frozen', to='frozen', refused=<attempted status>)
decision_status.blocked_writer: protocol layer only: the attention stall chain is the single convergence point
decision_status.frozen_release: frozen is an absorbing state (issue #1467): it is left only by the authorized approval close — a resolved attention record of kind=approval through the trusted-human path (the only _set_decision_status call that carries unfreeze_authority='approval'). Every other writer — a stall escalation, a non-approval resolve, a tool close, any future writer — is refused at the single decision_status writer: the state stays frozen and the attempt is audited as a refused decision_status_history entry (from='frozen', to='frozen', refused=<attempted status>). The refusal is a state invariant, not a policy gate — it holds with the protocol switch off too

constants_ref: mcp/common/constants.py: ATTENTION_STALL_BLOCKED / ATTENTION_STALL_FROZEN / DECISION_STATUS_VALUES / DEFAULT_DECISION_STATUS (test_protocol_guard.py asserts the two agree)
